source: office/EXPERIMENTS.md (the expectation and the kill rule are fixed there; this is the machine copy)
note: loop_daily.py reads 'feeds' to know which journal rows count for each experiment and rewrites 'running' on every run. Edit everything except 'running' by hand, together with EXPERIMENTS.md.

experiments.title: TP1 sized by volatility
experiments.rule: TP1 = 0.75 x ATR(15m) at the fill, min 15, max 60 pts, break-even after +15
experiments.expectation: More dollars per trade than the fixed +15 in NY
experiments.killIf: Net per trade is not above the fixed target's, or full stops per 10 trades rise by more than 1

feeds.how: phase 'resolve' rows with session ny and state 'resolved'; value = sum of shadow.beAfterNetUsd - live.netUsd

running.note: value = shadow (break-even after +15) net minus live net, summed over resolved NY cases; 21 resolve rows in all sessions, 10 of them unresolved

experiments.title: Early exit of trades that never work
experiments.rule: After 120 s, at -10 pts, if never seen +3: close at market
experiments.expectation: Smaller average loss; few exits that would have reached TP1
experiments.killIf: More than 1 in 4 early exits would have reached TP1, or net effect is negative

feeds.how: n = early_adverse_exit rows with decision 'exit' and orderSent; value from the early_adverse_shadow result of each: wouldHaveHitStop = (stopPts - |exitPts|) x contracts x $2 saved, wouldHaveHitTp1 = (tp1Pts + |exitPts|) x contracts x $2 given up, unresolved = not counted

running.note: n = live early exits; value = dollars saved (+) or given up (-) against the stop / TP1 the trade had, from the 1 exits whose shadow resolved (0 would have hit TP1)

experiments.title: Asia / London: all contracts out at TP1
experiments.rule: No runner in Asia and London: every contract leaves at TP1
experiments.expectation: More dollars per winning trade than the old runner rule
experiments.killIf: Average is below what the old rule would have paid on the same trades

feeds.how: runner_rule rows with mode 'allAtTp1' joined to the ledger; n = those trades that reached TP1; value = their average net dollars

running.note: n = trades under the rule that reached TP1 (21 fills carried the rule); value = average net dollars of those trades. What the old runner rule would have paid on the same trades is not in the journal, so the kill rule cannot be judged by this tool

experiments.title: NY runner by ATR
experiments.rule: NY runner: stop 2 pts beyond the entry, target 2.0 x ATR(15m)
experiments.expectation: Runner pays more than the old fixed runner
experiments.verdictAt: 20 live NY trades with a runner
experiments.killIf: Runner net is below the old rule's on the same trades

feeds.how: runner_rule rows with mode 'atrTarget' joined to the ledger; n = those trades that reached TP1 (so had a runner); value = their average net dollars

running.note: n = trades under the rule that reached TP1 (2 fills carried the rule); value = average net dollars of those trades. What the old runner rule would have paid on the same trades is not in the journal, so the kill rule cannot be judged by this tool

experiments.title: Control score by the indicator's formula
experiments.rule: levelsParity: pine (15m control score computed as the indicator does)
experiments.expectation: More entries pass the 15m control gate; the added entries are not worse than the rest
experiments.verdictAt: 20 trades that the old formula would have blocked
experiments.killIf: Those trades lose more per trade than the rest

feeds.how: needs the old formula's score next to the new one on each entry; the journal does not carry it after the switch, so n stays unknown until the bot writes both

running.note: n = entries whose two control scores disagree about the 0.22 line; value = their summed net. All rows with the second score: 49 agree, 17 disagree, 49 not computed; entries: 0 agree, 0 disagree, 0 not computed. 'Not computed' means the row was far from the line (controlAltWhy not-near-line): absence of controlDisagree is read as agreement only when the second score is present, and disagreements beyond 0.15 from the line are not seen

experiments.title: Stand down 30 min after a full stop (Asia / London)
experiments.rule: Same side, 30 minutes after a full stop, Asia and London only. NOT a bot rule: the trades are still taken and counted
experiments.unit: usd, the trades a stand-down would have skipped
experiments.expectation: The Asia / London same-side trades entered within 30 min of a full stop keep losing money as a group; the NY ones keep making money
experiments.killIf: The next 20 Asia + London cases net zero or better

feeds.how: ledger trades whose entry is 0-30 min after the exit of an earlier same-side full stop, session asia or london, entered at or after startedAtUtc; n = their count, value = their summed net; NY is reported beside it as context only

running.note: n = trades entered on the same side within 30 min after a full stop, in asia / london, since the start time; value = their summed net (what a stand-down would have skipped). Context only, the rule leaves it out: other sessions 0 trades, $0.00

experiments.title: NY late session shadow counter (09:00 PT on)
experiments.rule: NY trades entered at or after 09:00 PT, counted only; nothing is skipped
experiments.unit: usd, the NY-late trades a stand-down would have skipped
experiments.expectation: NY entries after 09:00 PT keep losing money as a group while 06:30-09:00 entries pay
experiments.killIf: The next 20 NY trades entered after 09:00 PT net zero or better

feeds.how: ledger trades in session ny entered at or after 09:00 PT and at or after startedAtUtc; n = count, value = summed net; the 06:30-09:00 trades are shown beside it as context

running.note: shadow counter, nothing is skipped: n = NY trades entered at or after 09:00 PT since the start time; value = their summed net. Context: NY entered 06:30-09:00 PT since then: 2 trades, +$277.68

experiments.title: NY runner profit lock ladder (+50/+75/+100/+150 lock +25/+45/+65/+110)
experiments.rule: Four steps: best price +50 / +75 / +100 / +150 pts from the entry moves the runner stop to entry +25 / +45 / +65 / +110; never loosens; TP2 unchanged; mode on / log / off (edge r1.6)
experiments.started: r1.6 installed by Mac 2026-11-12 (backup stamp 05:17:47, server clock)
experiments.unit: usd, summed broker net of the NY runners with a lock armed
experiments.expectation: Runners that reach +50 and come back leave with a locked share instead of the +2 stop
experiments.verdictAt: 20 NY runners with a lock step armed
experiments.killIf: Mac's rule: TP2 cuts alone do not kill it. At 20 cases net against the +2 stop, split by lock step and exit reason, goes to Mac to keep, loosen or drop. Offline estimate about -$500 to -$630 per 20 runners against the old +10 rule (an estimate, not a result)

feeds.how: ledger rules.runnerLock / rules.runnerExit (rows runner_lock once per journalId and step, runner_exit once per journalId); n = NY runners with a lock step armed; exits split by reason; money = broker net; TP2 winners cut = lock-stopped trades whose later price samples reached TP2

running.note: n = NY runners with a lock step armed (modes none yet; the exit row's lockStep is the authority, a lost runner_lock row still counts); value = their summed BROKER net. Exits: 0 tp2, 0 runner_stop, 0 profit_lock, 0 profit_lock_market, 0 with no runner_exit row. Lock ladder: no runner_lock row yet. TP2 winners cut (price samples reached TP2 after the lock exit; a lower bound, samples are last prices, not highs): 0 stopped by the lock. The second kill clause (net against the +2 stop on the same trades) is not computable: the journal does not carry that counterfactual
